subject: Request: Jurisdictional Subprocessor Map & Data Residency Evidence
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@halcyonlabs.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@halcyonlabs.com>, security@halcyonlabs.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Subprocessor jurisdictional inventory + residency evidence request

Hi Aditya,

Following up from our procurement call — Halcyon is scoping an integration with Redwood and procurement needs a granular subprocessor inventory that includes:

- Name of subprocessor
- Primary service (e.g., metrics, CDN, analytics, KMS)
- Physical jurisdictions where data is processed/stored (country-level)
- Whether the subprocessor can access plaintext customer data (Y/N)
- Type of attestation we have for each (SOC 2 / CAIQ / contract clause / none)

We also need a short data-residency statement for any EU customer traffic (we run in multiple EU countries) — specifically whether any caching, analytics, or support tooling routes EU-origin user data outside the EU.

Can you provide an evidence pack (spreadsheet + supporting attestations) by EOD Thursday (2026-11-18)? We can treat anything marked as commercially sensitive under NDA, but we need the metadata for our SIG/CAIQ review.

I attached the SOW and a brief list of in-scope systems on our side.

Thanks,
Raj

[attachment: HALCYON_SOW_Q1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@halcyonlabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor jurisdictional inventory + residency evidence request

Raj —

Thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. We'll assemble an evidence pack and deliver a preliminary roster and dataflow summary by EOD Thursday (2026-11-18). High level plan:

1) Preliminary subprocessor CSV with country-level jurisdictions and access flags (will include a column: "can_access_plaintext" Y/N).
2) Per-vendor attestation status: SOC 2 (type II), CAIQ snapshot, or contract clause note.
3) Short narrative on EU residency / caching / analytics routing for EU-origin traffic.
4) Links to redacted attestations (PDFs) or next steps where third-party attestation is pending.

For scope: can you confirm whether Halcyon considers EU-origin logs (support / telemetry) in-scope for the Rezzy integration? If yes, we'll include log-forwarding vendors explicitly.

Cc-ing Marissa (security) and Ben (commercial) to triage redaction and procurement items.

—Aditya

[attachment: redwood_subproc_prelim.csv (text/csv) — preliminary draft, internal only]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:25:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor jurisdictional inventory + residency evidence request

Aditya / Ben — quick internal note on what Halcyon will need from Security/Legal:

- Make sure the CSV includes: vendor_name, primary_service, countries_of_processing (comma-separated), can_access_plaintext (Y/N), attestation_type, attestation_date, contract_clause_reference, contact_for_evidence.
- For any vendor in the EU or processing EU-origin data, include data location of backups and whether KMS keys are customer- or vendor-managed.
- Redact internal IP (implementation notes) but keep jurisdictional granularity. If a vendor refuses to provide a CAIQ or SOC 2, list the compensating controls and escalation owner.

Ben — can you confirm our NDAs/redaction stance for vendor PDFs? I recommend we push redacted attestations to a secure Share (link) and offer a call for any follow-ups.

I'll pull the CAIQ snapshot for our managed infra and a short note on caching behavior (we already have EU-local caches; need to confirm fallback paths).

-Marissa

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@halcyonlabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Interim: Subprocessor roster + EU residency summary

Hi Raj —

Per our timeline, attached is an interim deliverable. This is a verified inventory (spreadsheet) and a short EU data-residency narrative. Items still pending are two vendor CAIQ snapshots; we've noted expected delivery windows in the CSV.

Key highlights (short):
- We operate EU-local inference caches in Frankfurt and Amsterdam; EU-origin inference traffic is routed to EU pools by default and does not leave the EU unless a customer-configured cross-region routing rule is enabled.
- Support/telemetry logs: aggregated telemetry for service health is sent to our observability vendor (TelemetryCo) which processes metadata in the EU for EU customers. TelemetryCo does not have access to decrypted customer prompts unless explicitly escalated via support (rare; marked in CSV).
- KMS: customer-managed key option available for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys by default. KMS vendors and key-residency columns are in the CSV.

Attachments included: redwood_subproc_prelim.csv, redwood_dataflow_eu_slice.png, redwood_caiaq_snapshot_v1.pdf (redacted where required).

Action items for Halcyon:
- Confirm if audit copies of redacted attestations suffice or if you need raw vendor CAIQ/SOC 2 PDFs.
- If you want a walk-through, here's a 30-min slot: https://calendly.com/redwood-security/review-30 (pick Nov 18).

If you need anything sooner, ping me.

Best,
Aditya

[attachment: redwood_subproc_prelim.csv (application/csv)] [attachment: redwood_dataflow_eu_slice.png (image/png)] [attachment: redwood_caiaq_snapshot_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@halcyonlabs.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Zhao <emma.zhao@halcyonlabs.com>, security@halcyonlabs.com
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interim: Subprocessor roster + EU residency summary

Aditya —

Received the interim package, thanks — looks thorough. Two quick clarifying asks before we closure the SIG:

1) Does Redwood's caching layer or any default telemetry flow ever route EU-origin user content to a third-party analytics vendor outside the EU (simple yes/no and, if yes, which vendor and which country)?
2) Please add a single point of contact for security questionnaire follow-up (name, role, phone).

If you can reply quickly with 1) and 2) we'll mark the prelim as accepted and book the walkthrough if needed.

—Raj
